steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Urgh...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: That's enough, Patia.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: It's... not over...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Patia, right?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Most of the Gun-Knights have been reassigned to the envoys' village. Your mission is over.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I don't really get it, though. It's not like Andoain doesn't know who the most powerful guy in the Basilica is... Why the whole charade?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: He probably wanted to make sure he got an audience with His Holiness.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Hm? You were actually listening to Lemuen?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: This has nothing to do with that.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: He is free to settle his score.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: But that doesn't mean I'm letting him get away.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Sure. Shall we get going?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Once we get Patia settled in.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: How should we face this Revelation? These mysterious, indescribable moments; these ambiguous, yet to be explained urges; these unascribable, esoteric intuitions...

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Where will it lead us? What kind of choice does it want us to make? Or, perhaps, this is merely a hallucination caused by the fatigue of life?

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: But Revelation is called as such only because we willingly believe in it or were told to believe in it.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: We could even say that if we knew it to be absolutely temporal, even if we deconstructed it into ice cold, objective logic...

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Regrettably, man will still shine a spiritual light upon 'Revelation.'

Thus, when this cruel reality befalls us, the cowards can point fingers at the ambiguity of the Revelation, while the devout can repent their insufficient understanding. In any case, we can at the very least ascertain that we ourselves are not the root cause of everything.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Ah, Andoain. I was expecting you.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You don't seem surprised at all.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: I can't say this was the result of any particular manipulation. The greatest lesson that I've learned in life is that people always cross paths, no matter their intention.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But, in the end, we all have our own goals.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The guardian, keeper, and executor of the most supreme law.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The eleventh man to take the name of Yvangelista, the Patron Saint of Sacrifice and Unity, and to stand atop the Lateran Curia as the Apostle, His Holiness the Pope.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Why recite all these titles you do not believe in?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The girl does not remain in your grasp.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: She's still young. There is still much for her to experience.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Yet we are old. So old that we know our way around conspiracy, political machination, and internal strife.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: What will you do now? Will you use this fine gift you spent decades preparing on her?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I'm not foolish enough to stand in a young girl's way.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Even if she triggered some kind of 'miracle?'

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: No, this miracle is Laterano's. It belongs only to Laterano. God's grace has fallen upon us. There is nothing more to it.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Do you enjoy history? I love history. For history to become history, you generally need an origin point, and when some kind of variable is introduced to stir up the water and form ripples—those ripples are history.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: What of the object that was thrown into the water in the first place, then? Perhaps history does not care about it.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: And neither do I.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The girl called Cecelia will go where she wants and do what she wants. Some day in the future, perhaps the name Cecelia will be known far and wide—it could also remain forever in obscurity.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But that has nothing to do with you or me.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It has nothing to do with the both of us. We have a mutual understanding regarding that, do we not?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You make yourself sound like a kind grandfather sending his granddaughter away.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: This is nothing more than you getting what it is that you seek. You now get to explain this miracle. In exchange, Cecelia earned the right to leave this place.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: This cannot even be called a trade. She never had the right to choose.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: No, I never wanted to do anything to her. Laterano has stood for millennia, and neither should it nor shall it ever waver for a mere mixed-blood child.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I only hope that Apostles before and after you feel the same way, and that those expunged names were not erased for nothing.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: We cannot ask for too much. Sins shall always be sins. Only time can wear them down.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: And it wears them down to the point that no one remembers they were once sins.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I cannot cast blame on our forebears' cautiousness. However, neither shall I accept those sins in order to cover them up.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: So long as our mutual understanding stands, am I right?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Hmm... as I said, it is very boring to grow old. Thanks to all the things that we experienced in the past, we are always fearful, on the fence with just about everything.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The old don't have the luxury of 'possibility,' Andoain. We have no choice but to continue down the path that was already laid.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: A path that was already laid...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: That goes for you too. I know of your journey.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: My journey...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Right, I once journeyed... and I heard the purest of prayers and the most vicious of curses.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I stepped into sumptuous palaces and plucked my shoes out of bloodstains.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I saw shameless sinners beg for mercy, and I closed the simplest of caskets on innocent children.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It was always the same. Their cries always died down, and their tears always dried up, and I... I always stood there right next to them, attempting to comfort them.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I told them that salvation would come, as long as we believed.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But no, nothing ever happened. Not even the briefest passing glance.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The Holy City of Laterano has weathered every storm that came its way. How would a saint sitting in his soft armchair and the Sankta that know only to sing the praises of their own dignity know that there exist hardships in the lands beyond?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: All the hopeless penances, withered consolations, and deafening silences.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Do you know how heavily silence weighs on my heart?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I seek only an answer.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: We will never find salvation, will we?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: 'Salvation.' I often hear this word from the faithful, as though a sort of incomprehensible accedence, as though an ark that will rescue all the drowning.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Behold, our grand and glorious Lateran City. It is so splendid and magnificent, solemn and refined, with a perpetual aroma of vanilla and sugar wafting in its air.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: All of this is a reward for abiding by the laws. All of this is our proof of salvation.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Yet this paradise is only a paradise because of the harshness of the wastes beyond.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: We could have been a star in the barrenlands, a torch in the cold night!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Don't you dare say I'm wrong! Laterano is not some ancient concept that floats only in scripture! It stands right here and now! Laterano can save everyone!

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: She cannot.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: And why is that?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Because we are only 'us.' Because we are the Sankta of Laterano.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: And 'they' are not 'us.' 'They.' They conceal, they become disillusioned, they consign, they become disappointed, they struggle, and they hate.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: They themselves mold and shape their own enemies. A man-eating monster of both lust and disgrace, with the flames of destruction hidden in its heart.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Why do you think these lands have seen countless dynasties and nations come and go in the flames of war while the miraculous Laterano has withstood the test of time?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Andoain, they are Inferno itself.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: And you, you chose to leave 'us.' You left behind the virtues that shaped us under the stubborn belief that your water could extinguish the flames of Inferno, that your candle could illuminate the night.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Why seek my answer? You chose despair for yourself long ago.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Three times have I visited Laterano. For the rest of my life I wandered the lands beyond.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I've met many men and women, and I do not need the Lateran Pope to tell me how dark their hearts can get. Yet there is also a ray of light in them. A radiant, blinding light that I can never forget.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: That I will never forget.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I was set ablaze by the light. Perhaps the fire is destined to be extinguished the moment it is first lit, but I could never again return to the eternally radiant Laterano.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Yet this perpetual radiance is cold and distant. Laterano's light shines on only a select few, and its might exists only to project this image of fabricated glory.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: In that case, I would rather be the torch that burns by the feet of those who are freezing to death.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Even if its flame will soon be extinguished.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Andoain, flames are destined to be extinguished. You seek to turn this perpetual light into a flame, and the flame will meet its fate one day. When that happens, there will be no more light, not even a cold and distant one.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: If you shatter the twin moons in the sky, then those struggling in the cold night will do so in darkness. Left only to close their eyes. Light will ultimately become a fantasy, a lie of a dream. Would you call eternal night a kindness?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You despise the small size of this paradise.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But do you know how hard it is for a small paradise to upon these lands?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You scorn its small size, but have you ever considered that there are those who try to live an honest life? What right do you have to turn this paradise to tinder for that wildfire of yours, destined to be put out?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: This world is hostile to beauty. To allow this beauty to persist forever, do you know how much the Lateran people, countless Laterans, generations of Laterans have had to sacrifice?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Andoain, who are you to so handily deny all this with a few trivial words?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Preposterous.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: There are those trying to live an honest life in Laterano, but does that somehow make the lives of those outside any less real?!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: They hold out hope despite their hardships, they follow the scriptures and the laws, they believe that they can change their lives, and they look forward to the rewards for their hard work.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Mrs. Baelen from the rock salt and sundries store, Deacon Landi of the Tidal Chapel, little Sagre, who ties the ropes on their bells...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Tell me, is there anything wrong with their faith, with their hope?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Tell me, oh great and glorious Apostle, Pope Yvangelista XI, the great protector of our paradise and defender of history.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Why did Rocamarea deserve to be destroyed?
Answers.
Questions.
So this is the answer that I sought.
So this is the question that I wanted to ask.
Something has come loose.
Something that once had me tied up... for so long.
Something is roaring... struggling.
Yet I feel only at ease.
As though I'm bathing under the saliferous sunlight.
The gunshots rang out almost at the same time.
The law is carved into each Sankta's flesh and blood.
And one must pay a price to break it.
I knew that.
There is a bottomless abyss beneath my feet.
I've taken that step already.
A great force slams me into the wall, and the sculpted relief presses into my bones, with the statue behind me crumbling to the ground.
There is no question that it was the strength of a patron firearm.
Though Yvangelista XI's body is old and frail, he is far stronger than he seems.
However...
I try my best to open my eyes and make out his figure among the smoke and dust.
The old man is still standing in the middle of the Basilica, but there is no longer a smile on his face.
He looks even older than he did when I stepped into this place.
But the halo above his head shines as bright as ever—
'The law in our flesh and blood. The painful price to pay.'
Price...?
Then, I realized what the real question here is.
The halo above my head is not glowing any darker than it used to.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Both you and I came out of this unscathed. What a surprise. It's worthy of celebration, though.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I was prepared to pay the price.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You're a pious follower, Andoain. Perhaps that is because you were not born in Laterano.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: In Laterano, we don't believe in our faith, do we? We live as part of faith itself.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: We Sankta have been its prisoner ever since the very moment the halos above our heads started to glow.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It...? What exactly is this law that we... the Sankta believe in?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: What exactly... does it mean to fall...?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Throughout Laterano's long history, each apostle has had the authority to interpret the Commandments and derive from them new rules and decrees, even placing them above all others.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Laterano is built upon this law.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: All Sankta know: violate the rules, the Commandments, or the laws, and you must pay the price.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The fallen Sankta are no longer connected to all other Sankta. Their patron firearms reject them.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Fallen Sankta are no longer Sankta.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: What 'is' a Sankta?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: A Sankta cannot point his firearm at another Sankta. That is a Commandment, and it is also our instinct, just like how a man cannot bring himself to take a step forward off the edge of a cliff.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Of course, there are those who can, and it seems to me you have more than earned the right to speak to that end.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: What makes me different from her?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I told you the Commandments are instinct, and I told you the Commandments are interpreted. Surely, a man of your intellect can tell those statements are mutually exclusive.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If the law was constant, then the 'interpretations' that were added over time throughout our ever-changing history could never have been 'instinct.'

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Correct, but you are calling the wrong premise into question. The law is naturally constant... but our 'interpretation' isn't really as 'ever-changing' as you are making it seem.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Interpretation isn't a coincidence, Andoain. Do you understand?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You said 'the old don't have the luxury of possibility.'

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The law is much older than either of us.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The apostle does not interpret the law. The law interprets itself. Why do you think the law is capable of this?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Take a look at these—Oh, my apologies. I made such a mess here—these structures, statues, stained glass, the exquisite domes and frescoes all around us.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Do they seem like they have constructed a particular illusion for us?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Do you recall the 'Revelation?'

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If we knew it to be absolutely temporal, even if we deconstructed it into ice cold, objective logic...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Regrettably, man will still shine a spiritual light on it.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: There has only ever been one true law.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: —We are to continue our existence.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Who are 'we?'

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Follow me.

a.text: I follow the old man into the depths.
Everyone knows that the saints of old are buried under the Basilica.
They are the most knowledgeable and outstanding men and women in Laterano's long history. Their brilliant marble statues have no eyes, rendering them blind to those who pass by.
We head down.
Stela recounting the achievements of the past popes line our path.
Among them were the conceited, the noble, and perhaps even the crazed, but not a single one of them ever allowed Laterano to be besmirched. Now, they stand here in silence.
We head down.
This is where the oldest of saints lie.

They were the ones who plucked the Sankta out of chaos. They were the embodiment of all the virtues of mankind. All those who came after merely imitated them. The nameplates on which their miracles are described are dim and lightless.
We head down.
I do not know where I am.
For as far as my eyes can see, nothing here has never been mentioned in any texts or literature. I cannot understand any of this.
This should not be part of Laterano.
A low humming sound fills the entire space around us.
Strangely, I find myself flustered by all this.
It is not the answer that I sought. It is not something man is capable of establishing or interpreting...
It is not something that interpretations, analyses, debates, or reforms could influence...
It is not a matter of whether or not you believe in It, why you believe in It, or how you believe in It...
After all, this is an undisputable existence.
In such a manner...
It exists.
What is Laterano?
What are Sankta?
I see.
We are us only because—
It links us all together.
It molds us.
It is the criterion upon which all things are based.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The path you and I follow was paved by law.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The paths you and I have trodden both lead to the same destination.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It allows you and I to continue making our way forward.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: This is the path It has deemed as correct.
